S1.why: A bare label under the bracket, 5 CJK with the digit; 個 with spaces round the number, as the vocabulary's count string does.

S2.s: もっと保存しませんか
S2.why: 〜しませんか is the ordinary Japanese way to invite, warm and in です・ます; it says carry on, with no word for limit or price. 10 CJK.

S3.s: 無料の %lld 個を使い切りました。保存したカットリングは、このまま無料で使えます。
S3.back: free-of %lld pieces (obj) used-up. saved cutlings (topic), as-they-are free-with can-use.
S3.why: 使い切りました is how a Japanese speaker says a quota is spent; このまま carries both 'stay' and 'keep working' in one word. Vocabulary word カットリング for the items. About 37 CJK.

S4.s: カットリングを %lld 個まで無料で保存できます。
S4.why: Plain statement of what is possible, まで for 'up to'; 21 CJK against a budget of 22.

S5.s: 無料の %2$lld 個のうち、%1$lld 個を使っています。
S5.why: Japanese names the whole before the part (〜のうち), so the numbers are positional with the total first.

S6.why: Noun-ending (体言止め) is how Japanese feature rows set a bold line; short enough for one line with 5,000.

S7.s: テキストは %@ 個、画像は %lld 枚まで保存できます。
S7.back: text (topic) %@ pieces, images (topic) %lld sheets up-to can-save.
S7.why: テキスト and 画像 from the vocabulary; images take the counter 枚, which is what a Japanese reader counts pictures in, while text keeps 個.

S8.why: Japanese lists three names with the ideographic comma 、 and no conjunction, as Apple Japan writes this exact trio.

S9.s: 一度購入すれば、同じAppleアカウントのデバイスすべてで使えます。
S9.back: once if-purchase, same Apple-account's devices all-at can-use.
S9.why: Appleアカウント and デバイス as the vocabulary writes them; すれば joins the condition the way a speaker would. About 31 CJK.

S10.why: お支払い is the polite word apps use for the person's payment; 一度だけ says single and nothing after. 9 CJK.

S11.s: サブスクリプションも広告もなく、アカウント登録もいりません。
S11.back: subscription-also advertising-also not-existing, account registration-also not-needed.
S11.why: The も…も…も chain is the native way to deny three things at once; いりません is warmer than 不要です. 30 CJK.

S12.why: The wording Japanese iOS apps and Apple's own StoreKit Japanese use for Restore Purchases.

S13.why: 〜中… is the iOS Japanese pattern for work under way (ダウンロード中…), with the single ellipsis character.

S14.why: Price first, then the verb, as Japanese paywall buttons read (¥800でアンロック); アンロック is the one unlock word used in every key here. 7 CJK plus the price.

S15.why: The same verb as S14 without the price.

S16.why: The phrase Japanese iOS uses for Not Now: it puts the purchase off without refusing it.

S17.why: The label Japanese iOS gives its close buttons, in the dictionary form system buttons use.

S18.why: まるごと means the whole thing with nothing held back, so the room comes with it, and 自分のもの is how Japanese copy says 'your own' without a pronoun, which keeps the app's no-あなた address; the noun ending lands as a settled fact. 10 CJK.

S19.s: ご購入ありがとうございます。ひとりで続けている開発の、大きな励みになります。
S19.back: (honorific) purchase thank-you. alone continuing development's, big encouragement becomes.
S19.why: 開発の励みになります is how Japanese solo developers thank their buyers; ひとりで names the one maker without making it a plea.

S20.s: おかえりなさい。以前のご購入を復元しました。
S20.why: おかえりなさい greets someone coming home, the natural word for a returning buyer; 復元 matches S12.

S21.s: 無料の %2$lld 個のうち、%1$lld 個を使っています。
S21.why: Same sentence as S5 so the spoken and the written agree; positional numbers, total first.

S22.s: 保存したカットリングは %lld 個。%@ 個まで保存できます。
S22.back: saved cutlings (topic) %lld pieces. %@ pieces up-to can-save.
S22.why: Japanese has no plural, so the same form reads right for 1, 2, 5 and 21; the noun-ending first sentence reads naturally aloud.

S23.s: アンロックしました。%@ 個まで保存できます。
S23.why: Past tense announcement, then the new room; same unlock word as S14.

S24.s: 購入が完了しませんでした
S24.why: States what happened with the purchase as subject, so no one is blamed. 12 CJK.

S25.s: App Storeに接続できません。しばらくしてからもう一度お試しください。
S25.back: App Store-to cannot-connect. a-while after once-more please-try.
S25.why: The standard Japanese pair for a store that cannot be reached; しばらくしてから carries 'shortly'.

S26.s: App Storeでこの購入を確認できませんでした。
S26.why: Says the confirmation did not come, plainly and without blame.

S27.s: このデバイスでサインイン中のAppleアカウントに、カットリングの購入履歴はありません。
S27.back: this device-on signed-in Apple-account-in, Cutling's purchase-history (topic) not-exist.
S27.why: 購入履歴 is the word Japanese users know from the App Store for past purchases; サインイン and Appleアカウント as the vocabulary writes them.

S28.s: 無料版で保存できるのは %lld 個までです。カットリングを一度アンロックすれば、好きなだけ保存できます。
S28.back: free-version-in can-save (nominal, topic) %lld pieces up-to is. Cutling (obj) once if-unlock, as-much-as-like can-save.
S28.why: 無料版 is the usual Japanese for the free version; 好きなだけ is the everyday 'as many as you like'. About 50 CJK.

S29.why: A compact used/total pair under the title; the order matches, so no positional forms are needed. 8 CJK with digits.

K1.s: 無料 %lld 個を使い切り。タップでアンロック
K1.why: Clipped noun-ending fits a one-key-tall capsule; タップで tells the person the message itself opens Cutling to unlock. 18 CJK.

M1.s: カットリングをアンロック
M1.why: Object then verb, the shape Japanese Mac window and menu commands take (アップデートを確認).

M2.s: カットリングをアンロック…
M2.why: The same command as M1, with the ellipsis character because the button opens a window.

M3.why: Row label in the vocabulary word; its value M4 gives the count.

M4.why: A bare number pair fits 10 Latin and reads the same in Japanese; used first, total second.

M5.why: 〜済み is the compact Japanese status form for a finished state.

M6.s: 一度の購入で、iPhone、iPad、Macのカットリングをアンロックできます。
M6.back: one-time purchase-with, iPhone, iPad, Mac's Cutling (obj) can-unlock.
M6.why: Same unlock word and the same 、 list as S8.

M7.s: このAppleアカウントのiPhone、iPad、Macでアンロック済みです。
M7.back: this Apple-account's iPhone, iPad, Mac-on unlock-done is.
M7.why: Status sentence that reuses M5's アンロック済み and the vocabulary's Appleアカウント.

M8.s: 無料になる前にご購入いただいたため、アンロックされたままです。ご支援ありがとうございます。
M8.back: free becomes before (honorific) purchase received because, unlocked remains. (honorific) support thank-you.
M8.why: ため gives the reason the native way; ご購入いただいた and ご支援 are the polite forms a maker uses to thank an early buyer.
